recent_updates.summary: GitHub package firewall entered public preview for all GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers (including data-resident GHEC): an install-time policy gate that sits between endpoints (coding agents, CI/CD runners) or internal registries and upstream package repositories, inspecting metadata requests and downloads against a configurable cooldown period, GitHub Advisory Database malware and vulnerability advisories, and supply-chain checks such as attestation downgrades, with an exception-request workflow. npm only for now. Free during preview; metered usage billing similar to Actions planned at GA.
Dependabot now supports npm 12, pnpm 11 and 12, and Bun 1.4 for version and security updates (changelog title; body not read).
The Dependabot alerts REST API now includes dependency versions in alert payloads (changelog title; body not read).

Open source license compliance is generally available for GitHub Enterprise Cloud (including data-resident GHEC) repositories with Code Security enabled: an enterprise-wide license policy is enforced through rulesets with a 'Require license compliance results before merging' condition, pull requests adding non-compliant dependencies are annotated, a new Enterprise Open-Source License Manager role approves exceptions, and dependency graph and SBOM exports now include license data. Since the June public preview GitHub added audit log events, policy download/update APIs and a package compliance check API intended for coding agents.
GitHub improved detection of withdrawn Dependabot alerts so alerts tied to retracted advisories are resolved more accurately (changelog title; body not read).
Dependabot now supports anonymous organization-level private registries, so organisation-wide registry configurations can be used without stored credentials (changelog title; body not read).

npm trusted publishing configurations can now be given opt-in permission to manage dist-tags with short-lived OIDC credentials, so maintainers no longer need a separate long-lived token for tag changes after releases or rollbacks.

Repository administrators can now set the runner type, custom labels and runner groups for Dependabot version and security updates per repository (GA), extending the earlier organisation-level controls across self-hosted and larger GitHub-hosted runners.

npm granular access tokens gain a 'Read and write (stage only)' permission so CI automation can stage package versions for maintainer review without direct publish rights, reducing token-theft blast radius in the registry supply chain.

dependency_check.status: Active OWASP Flagship-adjacent project; maintained by volunteers with constrained capacity
dependency_check.nvd_api_key_issue: NVD 2.0 API is the only feed. Without an NVD API key v12.2.x hits HTTP 429 rate limits, retries 30+ times and can corrupt the H2 database (GitHub issue #8298). Treat the key as mandatory; cache the DB centrally (shared volume or internal mirror) and update once per day rather than per build.
dependency_check.how_team_should_use: Keep only as a free baseline in Java/Maven CI where no commercial SCA exists; do not position as primary SCA in client proposals. Prefer OSV-Scanner or Trivy for new pipelines and feed results into Dependency-Track.

dependency_track.latest_version: 5.0 GA (9 June 2026); 4.13.x remains on LTS-style maintenance
dependency_track.features: Continuous SBOM analysis (NVD, OSV, GitHub Advisories, Snyk, Trivy, EPSS), CEL expression policies, component hash integrity checks against typosquatting, horizontal scaling on PostgreSQL, durable execution engine, VEX/VDR, portfolio dashboards, notifications; v5 needs offline migration from v4
dependency_track.how_team_should_use: Standard SBOM operations platform for client engagements with CRA, EO 14028 or NIS2 obligations. Ingest CycloneDX from Syft/Trivy/commercial SCA, apply policies, produce VEX. Plan v4 to v5 migration windows for existing deployments.

cyclonedx.relationship: OWASP CycloneDX is the ECMA-424 standardised BOM format (SBOM, SaaSBOM, HBOM, ML-BOM/AI-BOM, CBOM, VEX, VDR). Dependency-Track consumes CycloneDX natively; Snyk aibom, Trivy, Syft, GitLab and most commercial SCA export CycloneDX 1.6.
cyclonedx.how_team_should_use: Mandate CycloneDX 1.6 as the exchange format in delivery standards; require AI-BOM (ML-BOM) sections for client applications embedding models or LLM SDKs.

scvs.name: OWASP Software Component Verification Standard (SCVS) v1.0
scvs.summary: Six control families (Inventory, SBOM, Build Environment, Package Management, Component Analysis, Pedigree and Provenance) at three levels; complements SLSA and SSDF.
scvs.how_team_should_use: Use SCVS as the maturity yardstick in AppSec assessments and RFP responses; map tool capabilities (reachability, provenance, SBOM lifecycle) to SCVS levels to justify tooling choices.

top10_2025_a03.name: OWASP Top 10:2025 A03 Software Supply Chain Failures (final release)
top10_2025_a03.summary: Expands the former A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components / 2013 A9 into build, distribution and update-process compromises. Mapped CWEs: 447, 1035, 1104, 1329, 1357, 1395. Guidance: SBOMs, continuous inventory, trusted sources, staged rollouts, CI/CD change tracking, hardened build systems, patch management.
top10_2025_a03.how_team_should_use: Re-baseline client AppSec programmes against A03: SCA alone is insufficient; add ingestion-time blocking (Firewall/Curation), provenance (SLSA, Sigstore), pipeline hardening and SBOM lifecycle. Use A03 language in executive briefings to justify supply chain budget.

market_trends_2025_2026: Reachability is table stakes: Endor Labs, Semgrep, Socket, Aikido, Xygeni, Arnica and Checkmarx all ship it; Cycode and Konvu push beyond to AI exploitability analysis. Buyers now ask for language coverage and accuracy benchmarks rather than whether it exists.

CrowdStrike-published packages), Shai-Hulud 2.0 (Nov 2025), CHAINDROP (400+ packages), Axios and LiteLLM compromises (Mar 2026), TanStack/Mistral mass campaign and continued npm/PyPI waves through July 2026. AI-generated dependency hallucination (slopsquatting): CSA research note (Apr 2026) and vendor studies cite up to 27% hallucinated package names from LLMs; Sonatype Guide MCP (Mar 2026), SafeDep MCP, Socket and Snyk Studio insert verified-package checks into coding agents.

Agent-era supply chain: MCP servers, agent skills and IDE extensions are the new attack surface. JFrog AI Catalog/Agent Guard (Sept 2026), Snyk agent-scan, Endor AURI, AIR ($50M, Sept 2026) target it. SCA is now evaluated as one pillar alongside SBOM lifecycle, third-party binary analysis and threat intelligence.
